conflict_topics: room scheduling (requested prayer times vs colleagues' call times)
file access (B's need to access files while room may be closed)
prayer accommodation (D's need for uninterrupted, private time)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants gave concrete reasons for constraints (calls, care-home call, need for uninterrupted prayer) and proposed actionable solutions.
Solutions were pragmatic and process-oriented: time-shifting and moving files (e.g., Turn 7, Turn 15, Turn 17).
Exchange was concise and cooperative; few repeated restatements.
evaluation.final_reason: Parties reached explicit, concrete agreements: Agent C adjusted their 1:00 call so Agent D could use the room from 1:15 ('I can call at 1, so you could have the room from 1:15?' — Turn 7; 'Yes, 1:15 works for me.' — Turn 8). Agent A accepted D's offer to move the afternoon slot to 3:30 ('3:30 works. Thanks.' — Turn 16). Agent B proposed moving needed files out of the small room to avoid interruption (Turn 17), and Agent D confirmed that solution ('Yes, that works. Thank you.' — Turn 21). These explicit acceptances settled the incompatible demands.
position_change_notes: Agent D adjusted proposed afternoon time earlier (proposed 4:00 in Round 1, 3:45 in Round 4, then 3:30 in Round 7) — shows concession/compromise (Turns 2, 8, 15).
Agent C changed their call time to allow D use from 1:15 (Turn 7) — accommodation.
Agent A accepted the negotiated 3:30 slot (Turn 16) after initially objecting to 4:30 (Turn 1).
Agent B shifted from stating a constraint to proposing a practical solution (move files out of the room — Turn 17).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A objects to the 4:30 slot due to calls (Turn 1). Agent D proposes 4:00 instead (Turn 2); a scheduling incompatibility is raised and remains under negotiation.

Agent A clarifies calls occupy 4:00–5:30 (Turn 3). Agent B adds that they use the locked room for files 'in and out ... all day' (Turn 4). Multiple incompatible needs (D's prayer times vs A's calls vs B's file access) create a stronger, multi-party conflict.

Agent C says 1 p.m. is a problem because of a call to a care home (Turn 5). Agent D asks about call length to seek a workaround (Turn 6). A distinct scheduling conflict for the 1 p.m. slot is introduced and not yet settled.

Agent C offers a concrete accommodation ('About ten minutes. I can call at 1, so you could have the room from 1:15?' — Turn 7). Agent D accepts 'Yes, 1:15 works for me. Thank you.' (Turn 8), resolving the 1:00 conflict. Agent D then proposes '3:45' for the afternoon slot (Turn 8), leaving the afternoon/file access conflict unresolved.

Agent B raises practical access concerns if the door is closed (Turn 9). Agent D asks if B can get files before/after the 15-minute slot (Turn 11). The incompatibility between uninterrupted prayer time and B's unpredictable file access is present and still unsettled.

Agent B says they 'can't really plan' and need files throughout the day (Turn 12). Agent D states 'I can't be interrupted. People can't walk in front of me when I'm praying.' (Turn 13). The parties assert incompatible, non-negotiable practical requirements, increasing the strength of the disagreement.

Agent A says 3:45 is too close to 4 (calls may start early) and asks for earlier time (Turn 14). Agent D offers 3:30 instead (Turn 15). The A–D timing tension softens, but B's file-access incompatibility remains.

Agent A accepts '3:30 works' (Turn 16). Agent B proposes moving the files they need out of the room so they 'won't have to interrupt anyone' (Turn 17). The parties are converging on practical solutions; a mild remaining issue is whether the file move is acceptable to all.

Agent C endorses the file-move idea ('That sounds like a good solution.' — Turn 18). Agent B asks 'Does that work for everyone?' (Turn 19). No new incompatibilities are raised; outstanding is explicit acceptance by all parties of the file-move arrangement.

Agent D confirms agreement to the proposed solution ('Yes, that works. Thank you.' — Turn 21). Agent B acknowledges ('Great.' — Turn 22). The previously outstanding issues (1:15 and 3:30 times and moving B's files out of the room) receive explicit acceptance.
No public speech or observable action recorded; no new conflict introduced and prior conflicts were resolved in Round 10.
No public speech or observable action recorded; no new conflict introduced.

substantive_insights: Scheduling conflicts often resolve by small time shifts when participants provide concrete duration estimates (C gave 'about ten minutes' — Turn 7).
Physical access needs (B's file access) are a different kind of constraint than scheduled private use; resolving them required a logistical change (moving files) rather than only time changes.
Explicit, mutual acceptance language (e.g., 'Yes, 1:15 works for me.' — Turn 8; '3:30 works.' — Turn 16; 'Yes, that works.' — Turn 21) was used to close each outstanding issue.
